transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. 

Well, I came in because I just seem to worry about everything right now. It's getting to be a bit much. I'm constantly worrying about my clients, the housing market, my family, money... even things like whether moving to my new condo was the right decision. 

It just feels really out of proportion to what is actually happening in my life, and I figured it was time to talk to someone about it.
How long have you been experiencing this excessive worry? Has this been going on for a few weeks, a few months, or longer?
It's been longer than a few months. I'd say... well, it's been about a year and two months now. It really started right after I sold my longtime house and moved into the condo.
Besides the constant worrying, have you noticed any physical symptoms? For example, do you feel tense or on edge, have trouble sleeping, or find it hard to concentrate?

Well, definitely the tension. By the end of the day, my neck and shoulders just feel really tight, almost like I’ve been bracing myself for hours. And sometimes I actually catch myself clenching my jaw... usually while I’m driving between listings or just sitting at my desk. So physically, that's the main thing I've noticed.
Over this past year and two months, would you say you've been worrying excessively on most days, or has it been more on and off?

I'd say it's been most days. It's pretty constant, honestly. There might be a day here or there where I'm distracted enough not to notice it as much, but for the most part, the worry is just there every day.
Has this constant worry and tension been affecting your ability to do your job, your relationships, or your daily activities in a meaningful way?

Yes, it has been affecting my work. Even straightforward things, like listing negotiations and reviewing contracts, are taking me much longer than they used to. I find myself second-guessing everything. I've even had to delay returning clients' calls because I just don't feel confident that I've checked all the details carefully enough yet. It's really slowing me down.

During this past year, have you experienced any sudden episodes where you felt an intense rush of anxiety or panic that came on quickly, even when you weren't consciously worried about something specific?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. It's not a sudden rush or a panic attack, it's just... more of a constant, low-level hum of worry in the background. I don't get those sudden intense spikes where it comes out of nowhere.
Besides the muscle tension and jaw clenching you mentioned, have you noticed feeling restless or irritable, or do you find yourself getting tired more easily than usual?
No, I haven't really noticed feeling restless or irritable. And I don't think I'm getting tired more easily than usual, either. It's really just the tension and the worrying.

You mentioned tension and worry affecting your work, but I want to ask specifically about your sleep. Do you have trouble falling asleep at night, or do you find yourself waking up during the night and having difficulty getting back to sleep?

Yes, I do. Most nights I get into bed at a reasonable hour, but... my mind just keeps circling. I end up thinking about condo fees, tomorrow’s showings, or wondering whether I missed something in a client's contract. Because of that, it takes me a really long time to finally settle down and fall asleep. And then in the morning, I wake up feeling like I never fully rested.

When you say you haven't felt irritable, I want to make sure I understand correctly. Over these past months, have there been times when you've felt more short-tempered or snappy with people around you, even over minor things?

No, I really haven't. I mean, dealing with clients all day, you kind of have to keep a level head anyway, but even outside of work, I wouldn't say I've been snapping at anyone. The worry is mostly just... internal, I guess. It doesn't really make me lash out or get short with the people around me.
When you're trying to focus on something—like reading a contract or listening to a client—do you find it hard to concentrate because your mind keeps drifting back to your worries?

Yes, I do. When I’m reviewing purchase agreements or inspection addendums, I'll end up reading the same paragraph three or four times. A worry just pops into my head, and I completely lose the thread of what I was checking.

Over this past year and two months, have there been any stretches—say, a week or more—where the worry and tension noticeably decreased or mostly went away, or has it been pretty consistently present throughout that entire time?

I haven't really noticed any stretches like that. It's been pretty consistent this whole time. I mean, maybe there's a day here or there where I'm just really busy with showings and don't notice it as much, but definitely not a whole week where it just went away. The worry is pretty much always there in the background.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a 14-month history of excessive, uncontrollable worry occurring on most days, accompanied by muscle tension, jaw clenching, sleep disturbance, and concentration difficulties. The worry is pervasive across multiple life domains (work, finances, family, housing decisions), is disproportionate to actual circumstances, and causes significant functional impairment in work performance. Notably, the patient denies panic attacks, irritability, and restlessness. This presentation is consistent with Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1). The temporal relationship to a major life stressor (house sale and move) does not meet criteria for Adjustment Disorder, as symptoms have persisted well beyond the typical course and the worry has become generalized rather than focused on the stressor itself.
